title: How Does Thread Depth Influence the Mechanical Strength of Dental Implants in Varying Bone Densities?
text: This investigation sought to determine the impact of thread depth on the mechanical strength of dental implants in diverse bone density environments. A total of 60 Ti implants with varying thread depths were inserted into synthetic bone models representing three different densities (0.18 g/cm(3), 0.26 g/cm(3), and 0.34 g/cm(3)). The study utilized a push-out test to assess the interfacial bond strength between the implant and the surrounding material. Statistical analysis revealed that the thread depth did not exhibit a significant effect on the push-out strength across the different bone densities (P=.078). Mean push-out strength values for deeper thread implants were recorded at 35.6 N for low density, 42.1 N for medium density, and 38.4 N for high density, while shallower thread implants presented values of 34.2 N, 41.5 N, and 39.6 N, respectively.
